title: Kobalos Malware Investigation
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential Kobalos malware infection in your organization's high-performance computing (HPC) environment. Kobalos is a sophisticated backdoor malware that targets HPC clusters and other high-profile systems. It provides remote access, terminal session capabilities, and credential stealing functionality. Your mission is to investigate the compromised systems, identify the malware's persistence mechanisms, and contain the threat. The malware exhibits unusual network traffic, maintains persistence through systemd services, and attempts lateral movement to other hosts in the network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential Kobalos malware infection in your organization's high-performance computing (HPC) environment. Kobalos is a sophisticated backdoor malware that targets HPC clusters and other high-profile systems. It provides remote access, terminal session capabilities, and credential stealing functionality.

Your mission is to investigate the compromised systems, identify the malware's persistence mechanisms, and contain the threat. The malware exhibits unusual network traffic, maintains persistence through systemd services, and attempts lateral movement to other hosts in the network.

Learning Objective: Gain hands-on experience in investigating a sophisticated malware infection in an HPC environment, focusing on service discovery, persistence mechanisms, and lateral movement.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) via SSH using the provided credentials. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring your organization's HPC environment, you noticed unusual network traffic originating from the target host. Your first task is to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services running on this host that might be responsible for this activity. You are looking for a specific service flag, such as payload-transfer.service.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Start by listing all running services on the system.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for services that are not part of the standard system configuration.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Check for services with unusual properties or those that you do not recognize.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Now that you've identified a suspicious service, you need to determine how it maintains persistence on the system. Investigate the system's startup mechanisms to find out how the service is automatically started after reboot. You are looking for a specific persistence flag, such as payload-transfer.service or its associated timer.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Investigate how services are configured to start automatically on system boot.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Check systemd service files and timers.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for any custom service files that might be responsible for maintaining persistence.

levels.title: Lateral Movement Investigation
levels.content: Your investigation has revealed that the malware might be attempting to move laterally within your network. Examine the system for evidence of file transfers or remote execution used to move between hosts. Focus on any connections to the next-target host (IP: 192.168.50.6). You are looking for a specific lateral movement flag, such as next-target.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Look for evidence of file transfers or remote execution that might indicate lateral movement.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Check system logs for connections to other hosts.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Investigate the payload-transfer.service logs for evidence of lateral movement.
